key_insight: Learned surrogates can emulate 3D resistive MHD turbulence over about one large-eddy turnover time, with UNet and transformer models achieving relative velocity errors of 0.018–0.053.
engineering_relevance: These models offer a potential route to reducing repeated simulation costs for astrophysical and fusion-plasma turbulence while retaining important flow and magnetic-field structures.
method: Compare a convolutional UNet, shifted-window transformer and Fourier neural operator.
Train autoregressively on 128³ decaying MHD simulations at Reynolds numbers 1000, 3000 and 6000.
Use single-step training followed by short-rollout training with a common stopping rule.
evidence_signal: Training uses 500 simulations per Reynolds number; public-benchmark evaluation reports 39% lower error than the best published FactFormer isotropic-turbulence result and one-third to one-half lower rollout errors than The Well's best baselines.
watch_item: Accuracy is demonstrated over limited rollout windows; longer-term stability and generalization beyond the studied turbulence regimes remain unestablished.
paper_title: Learned Surrogates of Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
